positions.as_written: Treat them as one structure for the purposes of orientation.
Identify the cartilage margin first when working on the medial wall, then read the footprint from it.
Treat a knee with posterior capsular injury as having lost the plane that protects the vessels, and plan from the injured anatomy rather than the textbook anatomy.
Assess the posterior capsule and the fat plane on imaging before planning a route.
Plan the tibial exit from the step down on the posterior cortex rather than from the joint line, because the footprint is defined by the step.
Consider which part of the range the patient needs restrained before choosing which part of the footprint to reproduce.
Protect the synovial sheath where the plan allows.
Where the corners are injured, plan the approach from the corner anatomy as well as from the footprints.
Plan revision from what is present rather than from the standard description, and 7.37 covers the rest.
Assess each corner before assuming a route is available, because the fat plane that carries the vessels may have been displaced or lost.
Where the posterior capsule is injured, treat every quoted distance to the artery as void.
Consider staging where the posterior anatomy is uncertain.
